title: Kid Dracula
subtitle: Konami · Game Boy

body: Kid Dracula is Konami's Game Boy platformer about a young vampire trying to recover his castle from Garamoth. He has forgotten most of his abilities, so the journey through eight stages gradually restores the powers needed to overcome its changing obstacles. The character and enemies turn Castlevania's horror imagery into a cartoon comedy, with a pirate ship, factory and volcano among the destinations. The player begins with a straightforward projectile attack, then finds that the familiar-looking hero can answer later hazards in increasingly unusual ways.

Recovered powers expand the form and reach of Kid Dracula's attacks, while others affect movement through the stages. Brief flight, reversed gravity and an umbrella introduce different relationships to an obstacle that would otherwise stop the little vampire. A bomb can damage enemies and remove selected walls. The gradual return of abilities gives the campaign a clear sense of development. The next stage tests what has been learned, then introduces another reason to reconsider what the character can reach or safely pass.

The Game Boy release followed Konami's 1990 Famicom Kid Dracula, revisiting parts of its playful world through another portable adventure. Large, clear characters help the jokes remain visible on the small display, while the changing locations give the restored powers different uses. Released in Japan and North America in 1993, it represents another side of the Castlevania family. Its monsters and castle belong to the same broad visual tradition, but the immediate attraction is the expressive young vampire becoming more capable one small discovery at a time.
story_headings: A small vampire remembers his powers
